name: Professor X
bio: Telepath, founder of the X-Men and of the school that bears his name. His dream of human–mutant coexistence is the moral axis of the franchise, and nearly every relationship he has is shaped by how far he is willing to bend ethics in service of it. The Krakoan era made him a head of state and finally put him and Magneto on the same side.

name: Magneto
real_name: Max Eisenhardt (long known as Erik Lehnsherr)
bio: Holocaust survivor and mutant separatist whose conviction that humanity will never accept mutants makes him the X-Men's most durable antagonist and, repeatedly, their ally. His history with Xavier is the franchise's defining friendship-turned-rivalry.

name: Cyclops
bio: Xavier's first student and the X-Men's longest-serving field leader. Emotionally guarded, defined by duty, and the centre of the franchise's most famous love triangle. His arc from loyal son to revolutionary (Schism, Avengers vs. X-Men) is one of the longest character arcs in comics.

name: Jean Grey
bio: Telepath and telekinetic; host of the Phoenix Force. Has died and returned more than any other X-Man, which has made her relationships (especially with Scott and Logan) a recurring site of grief and resurrection.

name: Wolverine
first_appearance: Incredible Hulk #180–181 (Oct.–Nov. 1974); joined X-Men in Giant-Size X-Men #1 (May 1975)
bio: Feral, long-lived mutant with a healing factor and adamantium skeleton. Joined the X-Men as an outsider and became its heart. His friendships (Nightcrawler, Kitty, Storm) are among the warmest in the line; his rivalry with Cyclops is among the most bitter.

name: Storm
bio: Weather-controlling mutant, former street thief in Cairo, worshipped as a goddess in Kenya, queen of Wakanda by marriage, and the X-Men's most frequent leader after Cyclops. A stabilising presence whose friendships are usually mentorships.

name: Nightcrawler
bio: Teleporting, devoutly Catholic circus acrobat whose demonic appearance belies the team's gentlest temperament. The son of Mystique; best friend of Wolverine; the character most often used to argue that the X-Men's faith in people is justified.

name: Kate Pryde
bio: Phasing mutant introduced at thirteen as the reader's point of view; grew up on the page into a team leader, headmistress and, on Krakoa, a pirate captain. Her relationships are a map of the X-Men's generational structure: mentored by Storm and Wolverine, in love with Colossus, in conflict with Emma Frost.

name: Colossus
bio: Siberian farm boy who turns to organic steel; painter; the team's conscience and its strongest body. Defined by his family (sister Illyana, brother Mikhail) and by a decades-long on-again, off-again romance with Kitty Pryde.

name: Magik
first_appearance: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (May 1975); as Magik in Uncanny X-Men #160 (Aug. 1982) and the Magik limited series (1983–84)
bio: Colossus's younger sister, abducted to Limbo as a child and returned a teenage sorceress with a Soulsword and a demonic half. Her relationships are shaped by the gap between the child her brother remembers and the ruler of hell she became.

name: Emma Frost
bio: Telepath with a diamond form; former Hellfire Club White Queen turned headmistress and, eventually, one of the X-Men's most important leaders. Her move from villain to protagonist (Generation X, New X-Men) is a textbook example of a heel-face turn that stuck.

name: Rogue
bio: Power-absorbing mutant raised by Mystique as a Brotherhood operative; defected to the X-Men in Uncanny X-Men #171 (1983). For decades her power made touch itself dangerous, which turned every romance she had into a problem of intimacy.

name: Gambit
first_appearance: Uncanny X-Men #266 (Aug. 1990) (cameo in Uncanny X-Men Annual #14)
bio: Cajun thief who charges objects with kinetic energy. Charming, untrustworthy, and the X-Men's resident rogue; his relationship with Rogue is the longest-running romance of the 90s X-Men.

name: Mystique
bio: Shapeshifter and leader of the Brotherhood; mother of Nightcrawler, foster mother of Rogue, lifelong partner of Destiny. Her relationships are the franchise's clearest study in how a villain can love people and still fail them.

name: Destiny
bio: Blind precognitive mutant and Mystique's partner of decades. Claremont intended the two as a couple from the start; the relationship was stated plainly on the page only much later, and became a central thread of the Krakoan era.

name: Beast
bio: Original X-Man, geneticist and the team's scientist. Oscillates between being the most humane member of the team and, in the Krakoan era, its most morally compromised.

name: Iceman
bio: The youngest of the original five, a joker whose powers turned out to be far greater than anyone assumed. Came out as gay in All-New X-Men #40 (2015), a development that reframed decades of his friendships.

name: Havok
bio: Cyclops's younger brother, plasma-projecting and perpetually in Scott's shadow. Their relationship is the franchise's main study of sibling rivalry.

name: Spider-Man
bio: Teenage science prodigy bitten by a radioactive spider; the first superhero written as a person with rent, a sick aunt and a bad week. His relationships are the engine of the book: every villain is someone he knows, and every love interest is someone his secret endangers.

name: Mary Jane Watson
bio: Actress and model introduced as a party girl and revealed, over decades, to be the most emotionally intelligent person in Peter's life; she knew he was Spider-Man long before he told her. Wife from 1987 until One More Day (2007), which erased the marriage from continuity.

name: Gwen Stacy
bio: Peter's college girlfriend and first great love, killed by the Green Goblin in Amazing Spider-Man #121 (1973) — the death usually cited as the end of the Silver Age. Her absence shapes every later Spider-Man romance.

name: Harry Osborn
bio: Peter's best friend, roommate and, after discovering Peter's identity and his father's death, his second Green Goblin. The friendship is the series' longest study of whether loyalty survives what people become.

name: Green Goblin
bio: Industrialist, Harry's father and Peter's archenemy; the first villain to learn Spider-Man's identity and the one who killed Gwen Stacy. His relationship with Peter is personal in a way no other hero–villain pairing at Marvel is.

name: Aunt May
bio: Peter's guardian after Uncle Ben's death and the reason the secret identity matters: for forty years the book's premise was that the truth would kill her. Learned the truth in Amazing Spider-Man vol. 2 #38 (2002) and handled it better than anyone expected.

name: Black Cat
bio: Cat burglar who fell for Spider-Man and was openly uninterested in Peter Parker — the inverse of every other relationship he has. On-again, off-again partner, occasional antagonist, and the most consistently written adult romance in the line.

name: Venom
bio: Disgraced journalist bonded with the alien symbiote Peter rejected; both of them blame Spider-Man for ruining their lives. Began as a horror villain, became an anti-hero, and has spent the 2010s and 2020s as a protagonist in his own right.

name: Doctor Octopus
bio: Scientist with four mechanical arms; the first villain to beat Spider-Man outright. Swapped minds with Peter in Amazing Spider-Man #698–700 (2012) and spent thirty issues as the Superior Spider-Man, which turned a rivalry into something closer to a shared identity.

name: Miles Morales
bio: Brooklyn teenager who became Spider-Man after Peter Parker's death in the Ultimate universe, then migrated to Earth-616 in Secret Wars (2015), where two Spider-Men now coexist. His relationship with Peter is a mentorship neither of them planned.

name: Captain America
bio: Super-soldier frozen in 1945 and thawed by the Avengers. The moral centre of the Marvel universe; his relationships are mostly about other people measuring themselves against him, and Civil War (2006) was the first time the universe measured back.

name: Iron Man
bio: Arms dealer turned armoured futurist; alcoholic, narcissist, and the Avenger most willing to make the decision nobody else will. His friendships (Rhodey, Pepper, Steve) are all tests of how much he can be forgiven.

name: Thor
bio: Asgardian god of thunder exiled to Earth to learn humility. His relationships run on a different clock from everyone else's — Loki is millennia old, Jane Foster is a mortal lifetime — which is the engine of the book.

name: Hulk
bio: Physicist who becomes a green monster under stress; the Marvel character most often written as the universe's problem rather than its hero. Nearly every relationship he has is with someone who has tried to contain, cure or kill him.

name: Black Widow
bio: Soviet spy who defected and became the Avengers' most capable operative. Introduced as an Iron Man villain; her romances with Hawkeye, Daredevil and Bucky are the main throughline of a character who is otherwise written as unknowable.

name: Hawkeye
bio: Carnival archer who started as a Black Widow-smitten villain and became the Avengers' loudmouth conscience. His marriage to Mockingbird and his sulking rivalry with Captain America are the character's two poles.

name: Scarlet Witch
bio: Chaos-magic wielder introduced in Magneto's Brotherhood, married to the android Vision, and responsible for the two most consequential breakdowns in Marvel history (Avengers Disassembled, House of M). Her relationships are about who she can be trusted around.

name: Quicksilver
bio: Speedster and Wanda's twin, arrogant and protective in equal measure; the sibling who never fully left Magneto's shadow even after Marvel retconned the parentage (AXIS, 2014).

name: Vision
bio: Synthezoid built by Ultron to destroy the Avengers who joined them instead. His marriage to Wanda, his dismantling and rebuilding, and his attempt at a synthetic family (Vision, 2015–16) make him the series' study of what counts as a person.

name: Winter Soldier
first_appearance: Captain America Comics #1 (Mar. 1941); as Winter Soldier, Captain America vol. 5 #1 (Jan. 2005)
bio: Cap's wartime partner, assumed dead for sixty years of publishing, revealed in 2005 as a brainwashed Soviet assassin. Took up the shield after Steve's death (2007–2009). The relationship with Steve is the franchise's defining story of a friend returned.

name: Hank Pym
bio: Size-changing scientist, founding Avenger, creator of Ultron, and the man who struck his wife in Avengers #213 (1981) — the single panel that defined him for the next forty years.

name: Wasp
bio: Fashion designer and founding Avenger who named the team and, after her divorce from Hank Pym, became one of its longest-serving leaders. Written early as a flirt, later as the adult in the room.

name: Loki
bio: Thor's adopted brother and the reason the Avengers exist (Avengers #1, 1963). Villain for fifty years, then reborn as a child (2010) and rewritten as a trickster trying to outrun his own story.

name: Captain Marvel
first_appearance: Marvel Super-Heroes #13 (Mar. 1968); as Ms. Marvel, Ms. Marvel #1 (Jan. 1977)
bio: Air Force pilot given Kree powers; Ms. Marvel for thirty-five years before taking the Captain Marvel name in 2012. Her history with Rogue (who stole her powers and memories) and her Civil War II stance against Tony Stark define her relationships.

name: Black Panther
bio: King of Wakanda, the first Black superhero in mainstream American comics. His marriage to Storm (2006–2012) and his wary alliance with the Avengers are written as matters of state rather than feeling.

name: Ultron
bio: Artificial intelligence built by Hank Pym that hates its creator with Oedipal intensity; built the Vision in turn. The Avengers' recurring extinction-level villain and the clearest example of a villain whose entire motive is a relationship.

name: Mister Fantastic
bio: The smartest man in the universe and a distracted husband and father. His marriage to Sue and his rivalry with Doom are the two relationships Marvel has been publishing continuously longer than any others.

name: Invisible Woman
bio: Began as the team's damsel; by the 1980s John Byrne had made her its most powerful member and its real leader. Mother of Franklin and Valeria; the one person Doom treats with courtesy.

name: Human Torch
bio: Sue's hot-headed younger brother; the team's teenager even in his thirties. His bickering friendship with Ben Grimm and his rivalry-friendship with Spider-Man are two of Marvel's oldest running jokes.

name: The Thing
bio: Pilot turned rock monster, the one member of the team who did not want his powers. The first Marvel hero written as tragic; his loyalty to Reed, who did this to him, is the FF's emotional spine.

name: Doctor Doom
bio: Monarch of Latveria, sorcerer-scientist, Reed Richards's college rival and Marvel's model for every villain who thinks he's the hero. Remade reality in his image in Secret Wars (2015) and was briefly, sincerely, an Avenger.

name: Namor
bio: Marvel's first mutant and first anti-hero, king of Atlantis, in love with Sue Storm since 1962 and at war with the surface world roughly every third year. Sat on the Illuminati and the X-Men's Phoenix Five with equal contempt for both.

name: Silver Surfer
bio: Herald of Galactus who turned on his master for Earth's sake and was exiled here for it. The cosmic conscience of the Marvel universe; his friendship with Ben Grimm and Alicia Masters is where the Galactus Trilogy found its heart.

name: Galactus
bio: A force of nature with a face, written by Kirby as beyond good and evil. His relationships with his heralds, especially the Surfer, are the only ones the character has.

name: Daredevil
bio: Blind lawyer with hypersenses; Catholic, guilt-ridden, and the Marvel hero whose love interests have the worst survival rate. Frank Miller's run (1979–83) made him and Hell's Kitchen the template for street-level Marvel.

name: Elektra
bio: Matt Murdock's college girlfriend turned assassin, killed by Bullseye in Daredevil #181 (1982) and resurrected by the Hand. Miller extracted a promise that she stay dead; Marvel kept it for about eight years.

name: Kingpin
bio: Crime boss introduced as a Spider-Man villain and stolen by Daredevil; the only Marvel villain whose central relationship with a hero is about mutual, personal destruction. Elected mayor of New York in 2017.

name: Punisher
bio: Marine whose family was killed by the mob; kills criminals. Introduced to hunt Spider-Man; every hero he meets has the same argument with him and none of them wins it.

name: Jessica Jones
bio: Former superhero turned private investigator, retconned into Peter Parker's high-school class. Alias (2001–04) built a marriage with Luke Cage that has been written as the most stable in the line.

name: Luke Cage
bio: Wrongly imprisoned man with unbreakable skin; the first Black superhero to headline a Marvel book. Heroes for Hire with Iron Fist, husband of Jessica Jones, and leader of the New Avengers in the post-Civil War years.

name: Doctor Strange
bio: Arrogant surgeon who lost his hands and became Sorcerer Supreme. His relationships are mostly alliances of necessity — the Defenders, the Illuminati — and his romance with Clea.

name: Cable
bio: Son of Cyclops and Madelyne Pryor (Jean's clone), raised two thousand years in the future, returned as a middle-aged soldier older than his father. The relationship with Scott is the X-Men's strangest father–son story.

name: Deadpool
bio: Mercenary with a healing factor and a broken fourth wall. Introduced as a Cable villain; his one-sided friendships with Cable, Wolverine and Spider-Man are the character's actual plot.

name: Apocalypse
bio: Five-thousand-year-old mutant who believes in survival of the fittest and has reorganised two civilisations around it. His relationship with Magneto is a philosophical escalation; on Krakoa he became a council member and a husband.

name: Jubilee
bio: Mall rat with fireworks powers who attached herself to Wolverine and became his second protégée after Kitty; later a vampire, later a mother. The X-Men's 90s point-of-view character.

name: Wolverine (Laura)
bio: Clone-daughter of Wolverine raised as a weapon; took his name after his death (All-New Wolverine, 2015). Their relationship is the series' best treatment of the gap between being made and being raised.

name: Thanos
bio: Eternal from Titan, in love with the personification of Death, willing to kill half the universe to impress her. His relationships — with Death, with his adopted daughter Gamora, with his brother Starfox — are the only things that have ever stopped him.
